subject: Creating a column that incrementally increases as another column increases

messages.author: 93841b2a2283ece9
messages.subject: Creating a column that incrementally increases as another column increases
parts:
Hey D-RUG,

Sorry for the awkward email subject line. I can’t seem to figure out how to do this and don’t really know what to call what I am trying to do either...
 

I have one column of numbers (colA) ranging from 1.56 to 1200. I want to create a second column (colB) that incrementally increases as colA incrementally increases. 


As colA increases by 10, colB increases by 2. But this should only happen after values in colA reach 20. Before that colB equals 2. 


So,


1.56 <= colA <=20, then colB == 2

20 < colA<= 30, then colB == 4

30 < colA <= 40, then colB == 6

40 < colA <=50, then colB == 8


…all the way up to 1200 where colB should equal 238 (I believe)

 

Does anyone have any bright ideas as to how to make this happen? Perhaps a creative function using a for loop? Thanks for any thoughts that exist out there!

 

Lauren

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Creating a column that incrementally increases as another column increases
parts:
Sorry, pressed send before i meant too. Here’s a quick solution:

pincus = function(A) {
  if (A < 20) {
     return(2)
  } else {
     return 2*((A - 2e-10) %/% 10)
  }
}

B = pincus(A)

The %/% operator does integer division, so that it returns the largest integer multiple of 10 that is less than (A - 2e-10). I subtract 2e-10 from A so this increments B only when A is slightly more than a multiple of 10.

messages.author: 8c8f0ca54c4a2459
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Creating a column that incrementally increases as another column increases
parts:
Michael’s right. Here’s a properly vectorized version that doesn’t require sapply, and a test:

pincus = function(A) {
  ifelse(test = A < 20, yes = 2, no = 2*((A - 2e-10) %/% 10))
}
dat = data.frame(A = c(1.56, 10, 15, 20, 30, 40, 45, 50, 1200))
dat$B = pincus(dat$A)

print(dat)

ifelse is a vectorized version of if() {} else {} so it tests each value. With this, you get:

         A   B
1     1.56   2
2    10.00   2
3    15.00   2
4    20.00   2
5    30.00   4
6    35.00   6
7    40.00   6
8    45.00   8
9    50.00   8
10 1200.00 238
